summary: Sumathi Ramaswamy is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. She studied at the University of Delhi, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Pennsylvania, later holding posts at Penn (~1994–2000) and the University of Michigan (~2000–2007).

Sumi Lee specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned an MA at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign under Alexander L. Mayer, and a PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles, under Robert E. Buswell Jr.

Sumitra Mangesh Katre was a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of London. He served at Sir Parashurambhau College, held a chair at Deccan College (1942–1971), and was a professor at UT Austin (~1971–1976).

Sun-Ah Choi works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Juhyung Rhi, studying with Richard Neer, Robert S. Nelson, Jaś Elsner, and Aden Kumler.

Sung Bae Park is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who completed doctoral studies under Lewis Lancaster. He was an assistant professor at Dongguk University, joined Stony Brook University in 1977, and founded the International Association for Wonhyo Studies.

Sungdoo Ahn specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. After earning a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, Ahn served as Director at Geumgang University and became a professor at Seoul National University (attested 2013).
Sungtaek Cho is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. Cho held a post at Stony Brook University and served as Director at Korea University (attested 2012–2013).
Sunhee Kim completed a Doctor of Philosophy in Performance Practice at the University of Exeter under the doctoral supervision of Phillip B. Zarrilli.

Suniti Kumar Chatterji was an Indologist and linguist educated at Scottish Church College, University of Calcutta, University of London, and University of Paris. He held positions at Calcutta, the Sahitya Akademi, and served as Government of India National Professor in Humanities.
Surama Dasgupta was an Indology and philosophy scholar. She completed her MA and PhD degrees at the University of Calcutta and earned a PhD from the University of Cambridge.
Surendra Man Bajracharya specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Tribhuvan University under doctoral supervisor Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya and co-supervisor Ranjana Bajracharya.

Surendranath Dasgupta was an Indologist and philosopher who earned PhDs from Calcutta and Cambridge. He held academic posts at Cambridge, Presidency University, Sanskrit College (Principal, ~1931–1942), Chittagong College, Rajshahi College, and the University of Calcutta.

Suryya Kumar Bhuyan was a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar. He was educated at Cotton University, Presidency University, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta, later serving as a professor at Cotton University (attested 1956).
Susan Andrews works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned her PhD at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Chun-fang Yu.

Susan J. Rosenfield is an Indology scholar who earned her PhD from Harvard University in 2004, having studied under Stephanie W. Jamison, George L. Hart, Kausalya Hart, Shaligram Shukla, Saudamani Deshmukh, James W. Benson, and Thomas Burke.
Susan L. Huntington is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She served as a professor at Ohio State University from approximately 1971 to 2013.
Susan Naquin is a Sinologist and historian. She served as a professor at the University of Pennsylvania from ~1976 to 1993 and held a post at Princeton University from ~1993 to 2013.

Susan Neiman is a philosopher educated at Harvard University and the Free University of Berlin. She held academic posts at Yale University (~1989–1996), Tel Aviv University (~1996–2000), and the Einstein Forum (~2000).
Susan Niditch is a religious studies scholar who spent her career at Amherst College, serving in the religion department from approximately 1978 to 2020.

Susan Whitfield specializes in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at SOAS University of London, she directed the International Dunhuang Project at the British Library (1993–2017) and joined the University of East Anglia (~2018).
